raw_response:
We need a graph with 15 vertices and minimum degree at least 6.  
The sum of degrees must be even (Handshaking Lemma).  
If each vertex has degree at least 6, the sum of degrees is at least \(15 \times 6 = 90\), which is even, so no parity issue.  

A simple graph on 15 vertices can have maximum degree 14, so degree 6 is easily possible.  
One straightforward construction: make the graph 6-regular (each vertex degree exactly 6).  
A 6-regular graph on 15 vertices exists because 15 is odd, but regular graphs of odd degree require an even number of vertices — however, here we only need minimum degree at least 6, not exactly 6, so we can make some vertices degree 7 or more to satisfy the odd count.  

Simpler: take a complete graph \(K_7\) on vertices 0–6 (each degree 6 within that set) and connect each of vertices 7–14 to all of 0–6.  
- Vertices 0–6: connected to the other 6 in \(K_7\) → degree 6.  
- Vertices 7–14: connected to all 7 vertices 0–6 → degree 7.  

This satisfies minimum degree ≥ 6.  

Edges for \(K_7\) on {0,...,6}: all pairs (i,j) with 0 ≤ i < j ≤ 6.  
Then edges from each k in {7,...,14} to all v in {0,...,6}.
